question: Which country's women marry youngest among our 12 countries?
insight: India's average marriage age is 21.4, up from around 17-18 in the 1970s. Even the 'youngest' marrying country today is significantly older than a generation ago.
source: Our World in Data / World Bank Gender Statistics

question: Rank these 4 countries by years spent in retirement (most to fewest): France, USA, South Korea, Japan
insight: France leads with 22.5 years in retirement, while USA gets only 17.0 years. a gap of 5.5 years despite similar life expectancy.
source: OECD Pensions at a Glance / Demographic & Economic Context

question: At what age do Italians typically leave their parents' home? Guess between 18 and 35.
insight: Italians leave home at 30.2 (2025), while Swedes leave at just 23.1. a gap of 7.1 years between two wealthy EU nations.

question: Which country has the world's lowest fertility rate among our 12?
insight: South Korea's fertility rate is 0.72 children per woman. down from 5.99 in 1960. That is the steepest decline of any country in our dataset and well below the 2.1 replacement level.
source: Our World in Data / Gapminder / UN

question: Does later marriage age correlate with higher or lower female workforce participation?
insight: The correlation is higher (Pearson r = 0.71, N=12). Countries where women marry later tend to have higher female workforce participation. Note: N=12 means this is suggestive, not conclusive.
source: Our World in Data / World Bank

question: Which wealthy country has the lowest life expectancy: USA, Germany, Denmark, Australia?
insight: The United States has a life expectancy of 78.9 years, which is 4.2 years below Australia (83.1). Despite having the highest GDP per capita in this group, the US lags on this health outcome.

question: Which country went from nearly 6 children per woman in 1960 to less than 1 today?
insight: South Korea went from 5.99 children per woman in 1960 to just 0.72 today. a drop of 5.27. That is the most dramatic fertility collapse in our dataset.
source: Our World in Data / Gapminder / UN
